Anthropic IPO Financial Research | Growth, Earnings Quality and Offering ScenariosInternal investment committee research | Data as of 2026-11-05 | Units: USD millionsThis material strictly separates two kinds of information: disclosed facts come from the Form S-1/A Anthropic filed on 2026-11-02 ([S1]) and the company's announcement of 2026-10-26 ([S2]); teaching scenario assumptions serve only to exercise the valuation framework and do not constitute offering guidance, a price range or investment advice. The IPO remains a proposed offering under the intended ticker ANT; this material has no confirmed offer price or share count.1 | Executive SummaryAnthropic's revenue curve is exceptionally steep across the disclosed period: FY2025 revenue of 4,585, up 1,087.82% year over year; 9M2026 revenue of 33,242, up 1,206.17% year over year. That growth is not cost-free: 9M2026 compute and infrastructure expense reached 18,808, or 56.58% of revenue; total operating expenses were 34,502; and the GAAP operating loss was -1,260, a -3.79% operating margin.The key to earnings quality is not the absolute loss but its composition: within the 9M2026 net loss of -104,039, fair value changes on convertible notes and similar instruments of 94,324 are a non-cash measurement; after excluding 3,255 of share-based compensation and 2,086 of non-cash charitable contributions, adjusted operating income was 4,081. The business is close to breakeven at the operating level, while the accounting result is still dominated by non-operating items.Disclosed (S1 / S2)FY2025 revenue 4,585, operating loss -8,0609M2026 revenue 33,242, GAAP operating loss -1,2609M2026 net loss -104,039, fair value loss 94,324Adjusted operating income 4,081 (non-GAAP)IPO proposed, ticker ANT, no confirmed price or share countTeaching scenario assumptions2027 revenue 70,000 / 90,000 / 110,000Operating margin 5% / 12% / 18%Pre-money equity value 600,000 / 900,000 / 1,200,000New gross proceeds 50,000, 3% fees, 48,500 netPost-money equity value 650,000 / 950,000 / 1,250,000Basis of preparationDo not subtract the 94,324 fair value loss from the net loss and label the result "cash burn", and do not describe the 4,081 adjusted operating income as GAAP profit. The former is a non-cash measurement; the latter is a non-GAAP metric after two add-backs. Cash burn must be read from the cash flow statement, which is not available in this material.2 | Financial BaselineItem

All three scenarios use the same proceeds and fee rate, so the differences stem entirely from the revenue, margin and valuation assumptions. Net debt data are unavailable, so EV/Sales is not used and no DCF fair value conclusion is drawn.5 | Risks and Outstanding DiligenceRisk

The staffing and diligence plan described in this section is illustrative only and does not represent Anthropic's actual internal arrangements.6 | Conditional Investment Committee ConclusionOn the disclosed basis, Anthropic presents a combination of high growth, operations close to breakeven, and an accounting loss amplified by non-cash items. The base case implies 2027 operating income of 10,800, a forward P/S of 10.56x and 5.26% dilution; the bear and bull cases stand at 9.29x and 11.36x respectively.We recommend proceeding only on four conditions: first, the compute expense ratio stabilizes below 56.58% with long-term contracts as support; second, the adjustments behind the 4,081 adjusted operating income are auditable and share-based compensation does not keep expanding; third, the split of fair value, interest and taxes within net loss is clear, and cash burn is disclosed on a cash flow statement basis; fourth, dilution and P/S are recalculated once a confirmed offer price, share count and net proceeds are available. Until those conditions are met, this material offers no pricing conclusion or fair value judgment.Sources[S1] Anthropic PBC, Form S-1/A, 2026-11-02 — SEC filing; summary financials p. 24, MD&A pp. 150, 159.[S2] Anthropic official announcement, 2026-10-26 — S-1 announcement.
